chunks: And with this chain of transmission, he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said to Musa (peace be upon him): O Musa! Remember My Will concerning four things: First: As long as you do not see that your sins are forgiven, do not occupy yourself with the faults of others. Second: As long as you do not see that My Treasures have been exhausted, do not grieve over your sustenance. Third: As long as you do not see the end of My Sovereignty, do not place your hope in anyone other than Me. And fourth: As long as you do not see Satan dead, do not feel safe from his deception.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things Musa (AS) was instructed to remember from Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi from al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* outlines four pillars of spiritual psychology, linking self-awareness to divine attributes. It teaches that focusing on one's own sins prevents arrogance toward others, while recognizing God's inexhaustible provision alleviates anxiety about sustenance. Furthermore, it underscores *tawhid* in reliance (*tawakkul*) and constant vigilance (*hifz*) against Satan's enduring deception.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 14. And with the same chain of transmission that The Commander of the Faithful (AS) said:

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said to Musa (AS): O Musa! Remember My Will concerning four things. First: Unless you can see that your sins are forgiven, then do not look for faults in others. Secondly Unless you see my Treasures finish, then do not grieve about your finances. Thirdly: Unless you can see my Sovereignty coming to an end, then do not place your hope in other than Me. And fourthly: Unless you see that Satan is dead, then do not feel safe form his deception.
